comment.narrative: 1. - Organization of up to two regional Roadmap coordination meetings. - Enabling taking stock of progress, information exchange, knowledge transfer and standardization. - Support to organization of local coordination meetings (up to 12 in total). - Development of biannual monitoring reports (up to two). 2. - Gap analysis of legal frameworks report for two beneficiaries completed. - Up to one regional workshop and one thematic workshop for beneficiaries organized. - Provision of on-demand expertise on legislative and policy updates. - Regional arms-law compendium updated. - Gender Coach programme started with one SALW commission. - Media Strategy Development Programme initiated with one head of the SALW Commission. 3. - Needs assessment of the border-police and criminal-police services of the Western Balkans in countering illicit arms trafficking completed. - Strengthened capacity of ballistics experts and investigators for addressing cross border firearm-related criminality. - Assessment of capacities of the Republic of Moldova, Ukraine and Belarus for selected aspects of SALW control with identified targeted interventions continued.

title.narrative: Assessment and Gap Analysis, including gender screaning of partners' legal frameworks, on SALW control and the level of harmnoziation with the EU and international legislations Developed.

description.narrative: The assessment came from the evident need for legislative and regulatory framework on SALW/firearms control in the WB to effectively regulate arms control. This will consequently enable compatibility of arms control laws and procedure in the WB and the standardization of SALW control procedures and practices.

comment.narrative: No assessment done prior to the Roadmap.

In the course of the project, six (6) gap analysis of legal frameworks were developed in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, Serbia and North Macedonia, looking into myriad legislation dealing with control of firearms and explosives, production and trade in military equipment, and weapons deactivation. The gap analyses were based on a detailed methodology developed by SEESAC in early 2019, and an analysis of the national regulations and plans for the harmonization with the EU Acquis. The approach of the analysis was discussed and agreed upon at a series of initial meetings held in 2019 with relevant representatives of the MoIs in each of the six jurisdictions

title.narrative: Improved cross-border detection capacities with regard to illicit firearms trafficking.

description.narrative: To reduce the threat of illicit trafficking of firearms by enhancing the capacities of the law enforcement and border police for further gathering, analysis, and sharing of information. Needs assessment of the border police and criminal police services in the Western Balkans will be conducted in countering illicit arms trafficking.

comment.narrative: A detailed assessment of the capacities of the criminal police to counter illicit possession and trafficking of firearms in six (6) Western Balkans jurisdictions has been conducted, finalized and endorsed by the respective authorities in 2022. The methodology for the needs assessment was developed by SEESAC in the first half of 2020. It described in detail steps to be taken by experts as they conduct the needs assessment focusing on three main thematic areas: analysis of legislative and strategic framework; assessment of the administrative and institutional capacities; and assessment of the technical equipment needed. The needs assessments were designed to be conducted through a combination of extensive desk research and field visits to the Criminal Police authorities in each jurisdiction.

title.narrative: A Regional Coordination Platform established (Regional coordination meetings organized) to enable taking stock of progress, information exchange, knowledge sharing and strandardization.

description.narrative: The regional and local coordination meetings wll focus on taking stock of progress and will information exchange, knowledge sharing and strandardization.

comment.narrative: Over the life of the project eight (8) Regional Roadmap Coordination meetings took place on a biannual basis, in person or in a hybrid mode, gathering between 100-150 participants. The meetings were an opportunity to bring together members of SALW Commissions from 6 Western Balkans jurisdictions together with the key regional and international organizations working on SALW control and implementing relevant projects, as well as the donors supporting these efforts to discuss and share information about work being conducted, obstacles encountered, lessons learned, existing needs and plans for further engagement
